title: Uniformly finite filtered cochain localizations and support
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Regard a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] on a cochain complex $K$ as subobjects in the abelian category of complexes; finiteness of this filtration means that $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, uniformly in cochain degree. For an optional fixed filtration interval $B$, and a property $P$ of cochain complexes, let $\mathcal C_{B,P}$ be the full subcategory of these uniformly finite filtered complexes satisfying $P$, also requiring $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$ if $B=[a,b]$. Its morphisms are filtered chain maps. The canonical graded maps are the cokernel maps of [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction], applied in the abelian category of cochain complexes. Let $W_{B,P}$ consist of maps whose canonical maps on every graded complex are quasi-isomorphisms. Define $DF_{B,P}=\mathcal C_{B,P}[W_{B,P}^{-1}]$ by formal category localization, with its canonical localization functor. If $P$ implies $R$, inclusion induces the canonical comparison $DF_{B,P}\to DF_{B,R}$, defined by the universal property of localization. Use the conditions $P_+$ and $P_-$ of being zero in all cochain degrees below some integer and above some integer respectively, and $P_b=P_+\land P_-$. For $S\subseteq\mathbf Z$, write $\operatorname{Supp}_{\mathrm{gr}}(K)\subseteq S$ for $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$ for every $p$ and every $n\notin S$. For an object $X$ of the unrestricted-cochain localization, this support condition means that $X$ is isomorphic to the localization of a representative with this graded support.

No generic uniformly finite filtered cochain localization for arbitrary abelian C. def-trf-finite-filtered-localization instead permits per-term finite bounds when B is absent. def-trf-bounded-filtered-derived-category specializes to pro-etale module sheaves and Ab and has no Lean declaration; it does not give the generic arbitrary-abelian-category interface. FiniteFilteredModuleHomotopy and TwoStepModuleDerived concern ordinary modules and two-step filtrations. blueprint_refs found only unrelated derived-comparison blueprint nodes.
